title: Earthquakes and Volcanoes: When the Earth Releases Energy

questions.question: The point on the Earth's surface directly above an earthquake's focus is the:
questions.rationale: The focus is the rupture point at depth; the epicentre lies on the surface directly above it and usually shakes most strongly.

questions.question: Which seismic wave travels fastest?
questions.rationale: P-waves are the fastest and pass through solids, liquids, and gases, so they arrive at recording stations first.

questions.question: Surface (L and Rayleigh) waves are notorious because they are:
options: The slowest but most destructive at the surface
questions.rationale: Surface waves travel along the ground, arriving last but rolling and shaking it with the greatest destructive effect near the epicentre.

questions.question: On the Richter scale, each whole-number step up represents about:
questions.rationale: The Richter scale is logarithmic: one whole step means roughly ten times greater recorded ground motion (and far more energy).

questions.question: Which statement about magnitude versus intensity is correct?
options: One earthquake has one magnitude but many intensities
One earthquake has one intensity but many magnitudes
Mercalli values are objective instrumental readings
questions.rationale: Magnitude (Richter) is the fixed energy of the quake; Mercalli intensity varies with distance and local building quality, so one quake shows many intensities.

questions.question: The Koyna, Maharashtra earthquake of 1967 is an example of:
questions.rationale: Koyna 1967 is the classic reservoir-induced earthquake, triggered by the loading of water behind a large dam.

questions.question: The Circum-Pacific Ring of Fire accounts for approximately:
options: 75% of active volcanoes and about 90% of large earthquakes
questions.rationale: The Ring of Fire hosts roughly 75% of the world's active volcanoes and about 90% of its large earthquakes.

questions.question: Which regions of India fall in seismic Zone V, the most severe?
options: NE India, Kashmir, Kutch, and the Andaman & Nicobar Islands
questions.rationale: Zone V — about 11% of India's area — includes NE India, Kashmir, the Kutch region, and the Andaman & Nicobar Islands.

questions.question: Mauna Loa in Hawaii is an example of a:
options: Shield volcano with fluid basaltic lava
questions.rationale: Mauna Loa is a shield volcano built by fluid basaltic lava flows with gentle slopes; Fuji and Vesuvius are composite cones.

questions.question: India's only active volcano is:
questions.rationale: Barren Island in the Andaman Sea is India's only active volcano; Narcondam is dormant, and the Deccan Trap vents are long extinct.
